correctness.rationale: Let u and v be the two adjacent centers and L_u,L_v their leaf sets. If u is omitted and at least two L_u leaves are omitted, neither omitted leaf can ever be observed except through u and u cannot force while two such leaves remain, so power domination fails; the analogous statement holds at v. Conversely, if u is selected or at most one L_u leaf is omitted, that side becomes fully observed/forced once the bridge center is observed, independently of the other side. Thus a set is power dominating exactly when each side satisfies its star condition. This Cartesian independence gives P(D_{a,b};x)=Q_a(x)Q_b(x), Q_t=x(1+x)^t+t x^(t-1)+x^t, with the total and minimum-set formulas. A fresh literal propagation replay for (a,b)=(2,2),(2,4),(3,5),(4,3) matched the predicate for every subset.
residual_risks: The factorization requires proper double stars a,b>=2; degenerate parameters are not part of the theorem.
